prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the scene is a narrow rocky canyon with a sloping pile of pale boulders in front and dark cliff walls rising behind; brighter regions clarify that the foreground rocks are within roughly 0.5–2 m, while the walls and upper ledges are several metres farther away. In frame 1, two partly cropped people fill the lower left and centre at about 0.5–1 m, with another person roughly 3–5 m ahead on the rocks; in frames 2–3, nearby partial figures appear at the lower edges while standing figures remain about 2–5 m ahead and above the camera. Frames 4–5 show a helmeted person near centre-left at roughly 1–2 m and several others clustered behind and to the right at about 2–5 m, with some mutual occlusion; the camera’s turn changes their image positions more than their apparent distances. The map makes near–far ordering, rock relief, and human silhouettes clearer than RGB alone, but absolute metre estimates are uncertain, black sky and distant cliffs provide little usable depth, and several people blend into rocks or have inconsistent brightness.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates people from the similarly coloured rock: two large, partly cropped people occupy the near foreground in frame 1, smaller people stand higher and farther ahead in frames 1–3, and a larger central person with several smaller overlapping people appears in frames 4–5. It supports left/right, above/below, overlap, and visibility relationships—for example, the near frame-1 pair are side by side, while the frame-4/5 group contains people partly hidden behind one another—but it does not encode metric distance, so rough ranges of about 0.5–1 m for the largest masks and 2–5 m for smaller masks come only from mask scale and RGB context. The masks show that the people ahead shift from the right side in frame 1 toward the centre across frames 2–4 and then toward the right in frame 5 as the viewpoint turns; body orientation is only coarse, though the near frame-1 people and the helmeted frame-4/5 person appear generally oriented toward the camera, while several farther figures are side-on or facing away. It reveals partially visible people that are easy to miss in RGB, but it omits rocks and equipment, truncates people at frame edges, fragments overlapping figures, and includes several tiny or geometrically inaccurate person masks, so arm’s reach and exact inter-person spacing are unreliable.
descriptions.pose: The pose map contains usable structure almost only in frame 1: a small cluster of keypoints near the upper-left foreground and a short torso/limb-like skeleton below it, corresponding approximately to the two close, partly cropped people seen in RGB. Those detections place the visible joints within roughly 0.5–1.5 m of the camera wearer and indicate that parts of the near people are within arm’s reach, but the sparse, disconnected points do not reliably identify complete bodies, facing direction, gaze, or whether either person can reach the other. Frames 2–5 are blank despite multiple visible people, so the map supplies no dependable evidence about their separations, occlusions, approach or retreat, while RGB shows that the viewpoint turns across the rocky group. Where present, pose could make joint-level placement and partial-body occlusion clearer than RGB, but here missing detections, cropped bodies, disconnected keypoints, and absent hand skeletons make it the least reliable of the three maps.
